subject.title: Windows QuickStart defaults first chat to paid Anthropic model without credit warning

question: For Anthropic API-key QuickStart, should OpenClaw change the first-run default away from Opus, add a required paid-credit confirmation/preflight, or keep Opus and rely on improved post-failure recovery?
rationale: The source fix is straightforward, but the correct default and warning behavior affect provider positioning, first-run UX, and existing expectations for Anthropic users.

options.title: Lower-cost default plus warning
options.body: Use a safer Anthropic API-key first-run model such as Sonnet and still show concise pay-as-you-go billing copy before terminal hatch.

options.title: Keep Opus with confirmation
options.body: Keep the Opus default but require explicit setup confirmation that API-key usage needs paid Anthropic credits before the first terminal chat.

options.title: Post-failure recovery only
options.body: Keep the current default and depend on billing-error messages, usage/status surfaces, and docs to guide users after a failed first run.

recommendation.title: Lower-cost default plus warning
recommendation.body: Use a safer Anthropic API-key first-run model such as Sonnet and still show concise pay-as-you-go billing copy before terminal hatch.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the Anthropic default-policy change plus recent provider billing work.
